Split the conjunction.

- For the first part, use that multiplication of arithmetic functions is Dirichlet convolution:
  \[
  (f*g)(n)=\sum_{d\mid n} f(d)g(n/d).
  \]
  The two abscissa hypotheses give absolute convergence of both Dirichlet series at \(s\). Apply the standard L-series convolution/product theorem to rearrange the absolutely convergent double sum and obtain
  \[
  L(f*g,s)=L(f,s)L(g,s).
  \]

- For the second part, use the prime-power characterization of the von Mangoldt function. Since \(k\ne0\), \(k>0\), and \(n^k\) is a power of a prime \(p\) exactly when \(n\) is a power of the same \(p\). Thus exponentiation changes only the prime-power exponent, while \(\Lambda(p^a)=\log p\), so
  \[
  \Lambda(n^k)=\Lambda(n).
  \]
  Handle \(n=0\) and \(n=1\) directly if the available library lemma does not already include them.

The essential assumption is \(k\ne0\): for \(k=0\), \(n^k=1\), whose von Mangoldt value is always zero.
